fields.acceptance: go test -trimpath ./cmd/rhiza -run 'TestScripts/(land-commit|describe-golden)$' passes: land-commit.txtar lands an accepted change set with RHIZA_ACTOR set and rhiza land --commit --json, then git log -1 --format=%(trailers) shows Change: <the change set> and Actor: <that actor's handle>, git status --porcelain .rhiza is empty, and a file staged outside .rhiza before the land is still staged and not in the commit; (failure case) rhiza land --commit on a draft change set exits non-zero with HEAD unchanged and nothing committed; (failure case) rhiza land --commit --dry-run is a usage error with nothing landed or committed; describe-golden.txtar is regenerated with the new land request type. And go test -trimpath ./internal/api -run TestLandCommitViaHead passes: with SHIP_HEAD_RHIZA naming a head build that is not the running binary and ctx.Exec a fake head that records its argv and lands and renders in-process, land with commit set runs land and render through the head with no --commit in either argv, and then HEAD is a new commit of only .rhiza with Change: and Actor: trailers; (failure case) when the fake head's land exits non-zero, land with commit set returns an error, HEAD is unchanged and nothing is committed
fields.must_not: Change rhiza land without --commit, or the other lifecycle verbs' requests; forward --commit to the head build or change the arguments runViaHead forwards (internal/api/ship_build.go); commit anything outside .rhiza; push; change ship land's own commit (internal/api/ship_close.go); change handCommits' attribution rule
fields.statement: rhiza land --commit lands the change set, renders, stages .rhiza and commits only .rhiza with the message 'Land and render the change set' and the trailers 'Change: <change set ID>' and 'Actor: <actor handle>' (the actor the land entry was written as, resolved as every write resolves it: RHIZA_ACTOR, else git's user.email; its ID when it has no handle), all in one trailer block; without --commit land behaves as today. When SHIP_HEAD_RHIZA names a head build other than the running binary (as bugfix and ship-rhiza set in [env]), the land and the render still run through that head (runViaHead, its forwarded arguments unchanged: --commit is never forwarded), and the running rhiza makes the commit in-process after the head's land and render return, so a head built without --commit lands the same way; a failed head land or render commits nothing
